q-34153:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statements I and III are false, while statement II is true.

q-74650:
The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 1 & k+1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 1 & k+1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 4 \\ 0 & k-2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The corresponding system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x+6y=4 \\  & (k-2)y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=2,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y.$ So, we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x+6y=4.$  

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=2.$

q-131720:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have two free variables, $y$ and $z.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement III is true.
